The famous ship that sank in 1912 after hitting an iceberg is the RMS Titanic.

To understand the complex concept of blockchain technology provided in the text, we can use the analogy of a shared, public notebook. Imagine a classroom where every student has an identical notebook. Instead of one person writing in a single book that could be lost or altered secretly, everyone writes down every transaction or entry in their own copy.

When a new entry is made, it is broadcast to the entire class. Before anyone accepts the new page, the other students check their own notebooks to ensure the new entry makes sense and hasn't been tampered with. If the majority of students agree that the entry is valid, they all add it to their notebooks. Because every student has a copy, no single person can secretly erase or change a past entry without everyone else noticing and rejecting the change. This collective agreement and the fact that the record is duplicated across many places make the information extremely secure and trustworthy, just like the decentralized and immutable digital ledger described in the content.
